problems.title: Keep the forbidden denominator value
problems.question: Solve $14/(3z-12)-(z+2)/(z-4)=3/(8-2z)-5/6$.
problems.idea: Factor the denominators and multiply by 6(z-4), with z≠4.
steps: This is not the forbidden value 4, so it is valid.

problems.title: Solve a linear inequality with fractions
problems.question: Solve $3x-(2x+1)/2>4-(2-x)/3-x$.
problems.idea: Multiply by 6 to remove all fractions.
formulas: Multiplication by a positive number preserves the inequality sign.

problems.title: Restore a missing inequality in a system
problems.question: Solve $x-(x-1)/2>(x-3)/4-(x-2)/3$ and $(5x-1)/3-(x-1)>3x$.
problems.idea: Solve the two inequalities and intersect their intervals.
formulas: A system requires all its conditions simultaneously.
steps: Multiply the second by 3: 5x-1-3(x-1)>9x, giving 2>7x and x<2/7.
problems.note: The first inequality was lost in the converted PDF. It was recovered from the original Word file’s embedded equation.

problems.title: An absolute value cannot be smaller than its input
problems.question: Solve $|2x-0.5|\le2x-3.5$.
problems.idea: The right side is 3 less than the expression inside the absolute value.
steps: Therefore no x can satisfy it.

problems.title: Exactly five integer solutions at most three
problems.question: Find a such that ax+1<a²+x has exactly five integer solutions satisfying x≤3.
problems.idea: Separate the cases determined by the sign of a-1.
formulas: (a-1)x<(a-1)(a+1); dividing by a negative number reverses the inequality.
steps: If a>1, the solutions are x<a+1 and include infinitely many integers below 3. At a=1 the inequality 0<0 has no solutions.
If a<1, the condition is x>a+1.
Exactly five integers at most 3 must be -1,0,1,2,3. This requires -2≤a+1<-1.
problems.note: The finite count is among integer solutions with x≤3. The inequality itself, when satisfiable, still has infinitely many real solutions.

problems.title: A diagonal perpendicular to a trapezoid leg
problems.question: A right trapezoid has acute angle 30°. Its shorter diagonal is 8 cm and is perpendicular to the slanted leg. Find the midline.
problems.idea: The diagonal makes 60° with a base.
formulas: In a right triangle, horizontal and vertical components are d cosθ and d sinθ; trapezoid midline=(a+b)/2.
steps: The small base is 8cos60°=4, and the height is 8sin60°=4√3.
The base difference is h cot30°=4√3·√3=12.

problems.title: Intersect three 45-degree bisectors in a rectangle
problems.question: In rectangle ABCD, AB=6 and BC=8. The bisectors from B and D meet the bisector AE from A at K and T. E lies on BC as drawn. Find AK:TE.
problems.idea: Choose coordinates so each angle bisector has slope 1 or -1.
formulas: Distance along a 45° line between (u,u),(v,v) is √2·|v-u|.
steps: Take A=(0,0),B=(0,6),C=(8,6),D=(8,0). Then AE has equation y=x and E=(6,6).
The B-bisector y=6-x meets it at K=(3,3).
The D-bisector y=8-x meets it at T=(4,4).

problems.title: Use a diagonal to find the inradius
problems.question: A trapezoid has both an incircle and a circumcircle. The base sum equals the circumdiameter and its diagonal is 20. Find the inradius.
problems.idea: Cyclic and tangential conditions relate its leg and circumradius.
formulas: Cyclic trapezoids are isosceles; tangential quadrilaterals have equal opposite-side sums.
steps: Let the leg be ℓ and height h. Tangency gives base sum=2ℓ, while the other condition gives base sum=2R, so R=ℓ.
In a triangle formed by a diagonal, sin(base angle)=h/ℓ; the circumradius formula gives R=dℓ/(2h).

problems.title: Construct a triangle from a side difference
problems.question: Construct a triangle given angle A, adjacent side AB=c, and the absolute difference d of the other sides AC and BC.
problems.idea: Turn the side difference into two equal distances and use a perpendicular bisector.
formulas: A point is equally far from B,D exactly when it lies on the perpendicular bisector of BD.
steps: Draw AB=c and the ray from A making the given angle.
For the case AC-BC=d, mark D on that ray with AD=d. Intersect the perpendicular bisector of BD with the ray beyond D; a valid intersection C has BC=CD=AC-d.
For BC-AC=d, mark D on the opposite ray with AD=d. Intersect the perpendicular bisector of BD with the original ray; then BC=CD=AC+d.
Keep each nondegenerate intersection satisfying the specified side difference. If d=0, use the perpendicular bisector of AB directly.
problems.answer: The valid intersections from these constructions give all solutions.
problems.note: Arbitrary supplied measurements may produce no nondegenerate triangle. If the sign of the side difference is not specified, check both cases.
